There is news from Waterford that the tails of ten valua- ble cows have been cut off while the animals were grazing in a field at Ballydene. Compensation has been claimed from the Crown. Mr. Kenny, M.P., was on Wednesday sued in the Lord Mayor's Court for a debt of £23. Thei hon. member did not appear, but an order for payment in full within a month was made, a committal to issue in default. WRECK AND Loss OF 31 LIvES.—A Lloyd's telegram from Adelaide, dated Wednesday afternoon, says :—The Mars has gone ashore in West Bay, and will probably be a total wreck. The captain and thirty of the crew were drowned. Two VEssELS SUNK BY Commit's.— The schooner Alert, of Belfast, and the Conqueror, of Ardrossan, came in- to collision in the Channel early on 'Thursday morning. Both vessels sank. The crews were landed at Belfast, with the exception of one man, who was drowned. Announcement is made—apparently officially—that the Pope has confirmed the appointment of Dr. Walsh, Presi- dent of the Maynooth College, to the Archbishopric of Dub- lin. The evening organ of the Irish Nationalists offers its congratulations that the enemies of Ireland have failed in their schemes. At a meeting on Thursday evening of the Oldham Limited Liability Association it was stated that at the end of this week 64 of the limited companies' mills would be running short time. The Rochdale operatives who recently struck against a reduction of wages appear to be gradually returning to work. ARREST OF A " DEAD " MAN. William Melbr, of Upperhulme, near Leek, the ingenious farm labourer who, it is alleged, succeeded last month in representing himself to be dead, in securing registration of the fatality, and in. drawing his funeral money, and who afterwards, it is stated, stole a horse from a farmer near Leek, has been captured at Bury, Lancashire. A DETECTIVE OFFICER SENT TO PRISON.—At Lancaster, on Thursday, Ambrose Williams, a detective officer, was sent to prison for three months for theft. He had, it age peered, obtained money from a number of persons, repre- senting that he required it for police business and would repay them. He did not pay any of the loans, and be also appropriated to his own use 30a given to him by a brother officer to discharge a debt. THE FLOODING OF A DIIRHAM COLLIERY.—The inquest was concluded on Wednesday 'at Newbottle, Durharg, respectieg the death of thirteen men, killed in the Margaret Pit, at Philadelphia, on June 3, by the inrush of water, in the old workings of Elizabeth Pit. The jury returned a verdict that the deceased died from gas admitted from the old workings, and that the holing into these workings was accidental, and no one was to blame, the old plans worked upon having misled the management. In the Lovat peerage claim, which again came before the House of Lords on Wednesday, the case for the petitioner was closed, and Sir Farrar Hersche:l opened the case for the present Lord Lovat. On Thursday the Committee for Privi- leges gave judgment in the Lovat peerage case, the unani- mous decision of their Lordships being against the Welsh claimant. • The formal resolution passed was that in the opinion of the Committee John Fraser has no right to the title, dignity, and honours claimed in the petition. EXTRAORDINARi ELOPEMENT IN WALES—Great excite- ment prevails in the Rhondda Valley consequent upon the remarkable freaks of a faithless wife. A few years ago a large family of Welsh people emigrated from the district to America, where they appeared to be doing remarkably well. The elder daughter married an American gentleman, and about twelve months ago they tritertained a visitor from the old country at their home. After a brief stay the young guest eloped with his hostess, whom he brought back to Wales. On arriving in this country they were duly mar- ried, and took no their residence in the mining district of Dowlais, Rhondda Valley. Everything seems to have gene smoothly uatil a few days ago, when a gentleman, who lived near the family residence in America. came to visit some friends in the principality, and made a call upon the errant young lady during the absence of her spouse, and an arrangement was made for an immediate return to America. On arriving home in the evening the luckless husband found himself left with young twins, the mother being on her way to the New World. The occurrence has caused great sensa- tion in the principality.
